data.name: Gordhan
data.gender_notes: Gordhan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Gordhan is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Gopala’ which means 'cowherd'. This name is used for a boy and signifies one who serves, protects, and nurtures, just like a cowherd taking care of his cattle. The name Gordhan carries the meaning “Cowherd, One who serves” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gordhan usually hope their child will grow to embody cowherd, one who serves and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Gordhan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Cowherd, One who serves.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gordhan total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gordhan is deeply rooted in Hinduism and there have been numerous individuals bearing this name in different contexts in Hindu mythology. One of the most renowned figures is Lord Gordhan, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. In Hindu scriptures, Lord Gordhan is described as the destroyer of the arrogant king Mahabali, implying the name's association with important values such as humility and righteousness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Gordhan symbolizes the selfless, devoted, and loving nature of God as portrayed through the cowherd motif. The cow represents maternal love, care, and sustenance, while the cowherd is the one who serves, guards, and feeds the cows. Accordingly, the name honors the aspects of service, protection, nurture, and humility. Parents may bestow this name on their child with the hope that he will embody these virtuous traits.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gordhan: Cavernous Wealth. Symbolizes one who possesses an inexhaustible inner treasure. Spiritually, it represents the abundant grace of the universe that flows through the individual.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Gordhan was a renowned Jain monk and philosopher during the 12th century AD in India. The name Gordhan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Gordhan continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
